title: Cohomology of $\PP^n$, Serre 1954
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $X=\PP^n_k$, $\cO(m):=\cO_X(m)$, and
$S^m(V)$ the $m$-th symmetric power of $V=k^{n+1}$.

$$
H^0(X,\cO(m))=S^m(V)\ (m\ge0),\qquad
H^q(X,\cO(m))=0\ (q\notin\{0,n\}),
$$

$$
H^n(X,\cO(m))=0\ (m\ge-n),\qquad
H^n(X,\cO(m))=S^{-m-n-1}(V)^{\vee}\ (m\le-n-1),
$$

the two top-degree clauses for $n\ge1$; for $n=0$, $X=\Spec k$ and
every $\cO(m)$ is $\cO_X$, so $H^0(X,\cO(m))=k$ for all $m$ and there is
no higher cohomology. In particular (for all $n\ge0$)
$\omega_X=\cO_X(-n-1)$ and $H^q(X,\cO_X)=k\cdot\delta_{q,0}$.

Here $n,q\in\mathbf Z_{\ge0}$, $m\in\mathbf Z$, and all displayed equalities of modules mean $k$-linear isomorphisms (and the canonical-sheaf equality means an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules). Projective space and its twists are those of [def-pc-projective-space-twist]; $H^q$ is the Zariski module-sheaf cohomology of [pqf-def-cohomology]. The ordered basis $x_0,\ldots,x_n$ identifies $S^r(V)$ with the homogeneous degree-$r$ polynomials for $r\ge0$, and $W^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_k(W,k)$. We use $\omega_X:=\Lambda^n\Omega^1_{X/k}$, with relative differentials as in [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] and sheaf exterior powers as in [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power].

proof.text: The natural additive comparison of module-derived sections with the source H is linear over the base field. Apply its naturality to F.smulHom(globalSectionsRingHom(c)); the scalar-endomorphism theorem identifies its left action with multiplication by c, and the definition of the module structure on H identifies its right action with multiplication by c. Compose this linear equivalence with each source formula; a subsingleton source group gives an IsZero ModuleCat object. The nonnegative integer m equals the cast of m.toNat.

In dimension zero the single standard open equals top by iSup_standardOpen and uniqueness of the coordinate. Its standardOpenIso is affine space on the empty type of other coordinates, whose structure map is an isomorphism. Cancel the inclusion of the top open to deduce the structure morphism is an isomorphism. Glue the free twist generator on this sole chart to the unit generator 1: equality of two multiples forces equality of their coefficients. Apply the card-one cohomology formula for every integer m and the middle-degree vanishing formula for q nonzero, then transport through the linear comparison.

proof.text: For every n, including zero, compose exteriorSheafIsoExteriorPower on relativeDifferentials with canonicalModuleIsoTwist, using the ordered coordinate equivalence ULift (Fin (n+1)) ≃ Fin (n+1). The former compares the actual two sheafifications by identity on sectionwise wedges; the latter is the source canonical-bundle formula, with no positive-dimension hypothesis.

Map unitIsoTwistZero through source cohomology. The homogeneous degree-zero basis has a unique exponent, zero, since degree s = 0 iff s = 0. Compose its representation with Finsupp.uniqueLinearEquiv to obtain H0(unit) ≃ k, then with the linear comparison. For positive q, if q=n use top vanishing at m=0 (q≠0 supplies n≠0); otherwise use middle vanishing. Transport across unitIsoTwistZero and the comparison.
